assumptions.assumption: Module boundaries below aggregate adjacent files into change-safe units because the current repository mixes route, service, and rendering code inside large files.

execution_phases.phase: Freeze the repo boundary, identify the active slice, and record known blockers before changing code.
Resolve Telegram auth, admin rights, and the current User profile.
Apply entitlement, pricing, referral, and billing gating before report creation.
Persist or load Client and Report records, create ReportRun, and initialize ordered ReportChunk rows.
Build chart data, derived facts, and prompt context from engine outputs and profile payload.
Generate sections through template or LLM paths, validate content, and persist per-section state.
Mark report status, store usage/error metadata, emit analytics, and send best-effort bot notification.
Expose report/feed/admin state to frontend or bot surfaces and run diagnostics/scheduler follow-up.

flow.name: Auth and onboarding
flow.path: M-FRONTEND-WEBAPP or M-BOT-CHANNEL -> M-AUTH-IDENTITY -> M-DATA-PERSISTENCE -> profile readback.
flow.scope: Initial Telegram auth, profile completion, and safe profile echo.

flow.name: Report generation
flow.path: M-FRONTEND-WEBAPP or M-FRONTEND-ADMIN -> M-API-GATEWAY -> M-ACCESS-COMMERCE -> M-REPORT-WORKFLOW -> M-LLM-ORCHESTRATION -> M-DATA-PERSISTENCE -> M-OPS-AUTOMATION -> M-BOT-CHANNEL.
flow.scope: Create report runs, generate sections, finalize, and deliver notifications.

flow.name: Billing and one-off return
flow.path: M-FRONTEND-WEBAPP -> M-API-GATEWAY -> YooKassa -> M-ACCESS-COMMERCE -> M-DATA-PERSISTENCE -> checkout session/readback via M-FRONTEND-WEBAPP; partner reward and notification path stay best-effort.
flow.scope: Checkout session lifecycle, payment callbacks, unlock snapshots, and partner rewards.

flow.name: Daily feed
flow.path: M-FRONTEND-WEBAPP -> M-API-GATEWAY -> engine calculations -> M-OPS-AUTOMATION -> LLM fallback or live provider -> response.
flow.scope: Personalized feed context build, deterministic facts, LLM fallback, and response render.

flow.name: Admin operations
flow.path: M-FRONTEND-ADMIN -> M-API-GATEWAY -> M-DATA-PERSISTENCE and M-REPORT-WORKFLOW -> regenerated report state and diagnostics traces.
flow.scope: Admin queue views, section regeneration, diagnostics, and entitlement actions.

sequencing_rules.rule: Change auth or referral token formats only in one coordinated wave across M-AUTH-IDENTITY, M-ACCESS-COMMERCE, M-FRONTEND-WEBAPP, and M-BOT-CHANNEL.

Change pricing, trial, quota, credit, or one-off unlock policy only after updating config constants, backend enforcement, checkout-session/resume handling, /api/users/me report_unlocks/report_access exposure, and user-facing catalog/create/billing-complete screens together.
Change report section schema only with synchronized updates to M-REPORT-WORKFLOW, M-LLM-ORCHESTRATION, and all report render/read surfaces.
Preserve ordered chunk initialization before parallel generation; do not introduce writes that can reorder or duplicate section state.
Apply persistence changes additively first: schema path in M-DATA-PERSISTENCE, then ORM, then calling code, then UI exposure.
Do not make bot delivery a blocking dependency for report completion, billing success, or referral persistence.
Any admin UI change that relies on server-side fetch must be checked against the header-based auth contract before release.

Adopt the shipped per-report access snapshot across more frontend/admin surfaces so can_access_premium becomes compatibility-only rather than the primary premium gate.
Add per-module contracts and maps for the highest-change backend and frontend slices.
